title: Ponytail plugin explained: a 7-step 'does this need to exist?' ladder makes Claude Code write minimal code (3,629 -> 490 LOC on the same task) while never skipping security/accessibility

tools.name: Ponytail
tools.detail: MIT-licensed Claude Code plugin/skill; ~100k stars claimed; '#1 Repository Of The Day' badge on README

claims: Same task, same tests, same model: 3,629 lines without the skill vs 490 lines with Ponytail (author's own benchmark); on-screen bar shows LOC -54%
Security validation, data-loss handling and accessibility are hard-coded as 'never skip'
Lazy about the solution, never about reading the codebase
how_to_steps: Install the Ponytail plugin in Claude Code

Before writing code the agent climbs the ladder: 1 Does this need to exist? (no -> skip) 2 Already in this codebase? (reuse) 3 Stdlib does it? (use it) 4 Native platform feature? (STOP HERE) 5 Installed dependency? (use it) 6 One line? 7 Only then: the minimum that works
Example: a date picker becomes one <input type=date> instead of npm i flatpickr + a 120-line wrapper component
on_screen_only: README badges: MIT license, '#1 Repository Of The Day', stars ~153k, release v4.9.0 (small text, low confidence)
'Your agent over-builds it': npm i flatpickr +1 dependency / new DatePicker wrapper component +120 lines
Full 7-step ladder with verdict per rung (skip it / reuse it / use it / STOP HERE / use it / one line / the minimum that works)
'Lazy, not negligent' panel: Accessibility and data-loss handling hard-coded as never skip
Benchmark panel 'vs the same agent with no skill': LOC -54%, Tokens, Cost, Time, Safe bars; 490 vs 3,629 lines
